title: Carp Country, Cycling the Třeboň Ponds and the Vltava

bestPeriod.note: Late October is the carp harvest, when the ponds are drained and the dams are working roads; midsummer brings mosquitoes to the bog margins.

summary: Flat dam-top gravel through a 700-year-old fishpond landscape, linked to the Vltava cycle path and the climb into Český Krumlov.
hook: The Třeboň basin is a machine built in the sixteenth century and still running: 500 ponds, hand-dug canals, and dams wide enough to ride two abreast, all engineered by men whose names are still on them. It is the flattest interesting cycling in Central Europe. Then, on Day 6, the land finally tilts and drops you into Český Krumlov.

snapshot.Base(s): Třeboň (3 nights) → České Budějovice (2 nights) → Český Krumlov (2 nights)
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx 330 km, roughly 1,900 m cumulative gain; asphalt on the Vltava corridor, crushed limestone and packed sand on the pond dams, short grass and forest-track sections
snapshot.Getting There: Prague (PRG) → bus or metro to Praha hl. n., ČD express to České Budějovice (approx 2h20), local line to Třeboň
snapshot.Who It Suits: Riders who want long flat days, birdwatchers, families, and anyone who thinks a fish dinner is a legitimate reason to travel

itinerary.title: Into the basin, around Svět
itinerary.morning: Train from Prague to České Budějovice, then the regional line east to Třeboň. ČD charges a bike ticket of roughly CZK 45-65 (approx €2.00-2.60), plus a compulsory bike seat reservation of about CZK 35 on express services with a marked bike wagon.
itinerary.afternoon: A gentle first loop around Svět, the pond that Třeboň sits on. The circuit is 12 km of packed dam-top gravel and asphalt, past the Schwarzenberg family tomb at Domanín, a neo-Gothic mausoleum in a wood, open in season for approx CZK 120.
itinerary.evening: Třeboň's Masarykovo náměstí is an unbroken Renaissance square with arcades on both sides. Eat carp: Šupina a Šupinka near the Svinenská gate has been serving pond fish for decades and does a fried carp and a carp soup that justify the trip.
itinerary.dayStats: 28 km, +90 m, half packed gravel dam-tops, half asphalt.

itinerary.title: Rožmberk, the largest pond in the country
itinerary.morning: North to the Rožmberk dam, built 1584-1590 by Jakub Krčín of Jelčany for the Rožmberk lords. It holds 489 hectares of water behind an earth wall planted with 400-year-old oaks. The dam top is a wide grass-and-gravel road, closed to cars.
itinerary.afternoon: Follow the Zlatá stoka, the Golden Canal, 45 km of hand-cut channel finished in 1520 and still feeding the whole system, to Stará Hlína, then back past the Nová řeka diversion canal. Reed beds, herons, eagles.
itinerary.evening: The Třeboň spa houses, Bertiny lázně and Lázně Aurora, both sell peat baths and swim access to non-residents. After 70 km on gravel, take the peat bath.
itinerary.dayStats: 68 km, +140 m, roughly 40 km of crushed limestone and packed sand.

itinerary.title: Novohradské foothills and the Greenway
itinerary.morning: South on the Greenway Praha-Vídeň, the marked Prague-Vienna corridor, through Chlum u Třeboně and its glassworks village toward Nové Hrady. The land rises for the first time.
itinerary.afternoon: Nové Hrady has a Rožmberk castle, an Empire-period chateau and the Terčino údolí landscape park with its artificial waterfall. Return north on quiet asphalt through Borovany, whose Augustinian monastery has been restored as a cultural centre.
itinerary.evening: Last night in Třeboň. Walk the town walls and the Rožmberk brewery courtyard; the beer is Regent, brewed here since 1379.
itinerary.dayStats: 74 km, +410 m, mostly asphalt with 8 km of forest gravel.

itinerary.title: West to České Budějovice via Hluboká
itinerary.morning: Leave Třeboň westward on quiet field roads through Lomnice nad Lužnicí and Veselí nad Lužnicí, then pick up the Vltava corridor. Bags go ahead: Top Bicycle and AVE Bicycle Tours both run luggage transfer across South Bohemia for roughly €12-18 per bag per stage.
itinerary.afternoon: Hluboká nad Vltavou is a Windsor-style neo-Gothic pile rebuilt by the Schwarzenbergs in the 1840s; approx CZK 350, tours timed, so buy the slot on arrival. The Alšova jihočeská galerie in the old riding school is quieter.
itinerary.evening: Roll into České Budějovice on the riverside path. Náměstí Přemysla Otakara II is one of the largest medieval squares in Central Europe, 133 metres a side.
itinerary.dayStats: 62 km, +230 m, asphalt with 6 km crushed limestone along the Vltava.

itinerary.title: Holašovice and the Blanský les edge
itinerary.morning: West out of Budějovice through Dubné on lanes to Holašovice, a UNESCO-listed village of rural Baroque farmhouse gables around a green with two ponds. Twenty-two protected homesteads, still lived in.
itinerary.afternoon: Loop south under the Blanský les hills to Křemže and back along the Vltava. This is the first day with sustained rolling, and the return along the river is fast.
itinerary.evening: Budvar's brewery runs English tours at fixed times, approx CZK 250; the beer at source is noticeably softer. Otherwise the Masné krámy beer hall in the old butchers' arcade.
itinerary.dayStats: 58 km, +480 m, asphalt with 5 km gravel.

itinerary.title: Up the Vltava to Český Krumlov
itinerary.morning: The Vltava cycle path south from Budějovice is the prettiest riding of the week: a mostly asphalt riverside route through Boršov and Zlatá Koruna, where the Cistercian abbey of 1263 keeps one of the best-preserved Gothic cloisters in Bohemia (approx CZK 180).
itinerary.afternoon: Continue to Český Krumlov, arriving over the meander with the castle tower directly above. Push the last cobbled climb into the old town rather than riding it; the setts are polished and steep.
itinerary.evening: Krumlov after 18:00, when the day coaches have left, is a different place. The Baroque theatre in the castle is one of only a handful in the world with original stage machinery; tours are strictly limited and sell out.
itinerary.dayStats: 42 km, +360 m, asphalt with cobbles in the old town.

itinerary.title: Lipno approach and the train home
itinerary.morning: Ride the Vltava upstream toward Zlatá Koruna's opposite bank or push on to Rožmberk nad Vltavou, a compact valley castle 25 km south. Turn where the legs say.
itinerary.afternoon: Return to Český Krumlov and take ČD line 194 north to České Budějovice. The line runs a bike wagon through the summer and it fills on Sunday afternoons, reserve, or take an earlier train.
itinerary.evening: Connect at České Budějovice for Prague. Bikes need a ticket and, on express services, a reserved bike slot.
itinerary.dayStats: 40 km, +320 m, asphalt with 4 km gravel.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Bílý koníček
accommodationStrategy.description: The oldest house on the square, Renaissance-gabled, with an interior courtyard where bikes are locked overnight. Three nights here is the structural decision of the trip: the pond basin is a wheel with Třeboň at the hub, so you ride unloaded every day and the spa is a five-minute walk.
accommodationStrategy.booking: two months ahead; the October carp harvest weekends sell out in spring.
accommodationStrategy.priceNote: CZK 1,900-2,600 (approx €78-105) per night for two with breakfast

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Budweis
accommodationStrategy.description: A restored malt house on the Malše with a secure garage, a bike-wash point in the yard and a lift to the rooms. It is 300 metres from the main square and directly on the Vltava cycle route, so Day 5 and Day 6 both start without touching city traffic.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Dvořák
accommodationStrategy.description: Inside the loop of the Vltava under the castle, with locked storage and a terrace over the water. Sleeping inside the old town rather than in the modern outskirts is what makes the empty early-morning Krumlov possible, and it saves the cobbled climb twice a day.

logistics.emergency: 112 pan-European; in Czechia 155 for ambulance and 158 for police both work directly and are often faster.
logistics.money: Czechia uses the koruna, not the euro. Roughly CZK 24-25 to the euro in 2026. Pay in crowns, euro-accepting tourist businesses use punitive rates. Cards are near-universal; village pubs and pond-side stalls are cash.

other.label: Bikes on ČD
other.text: A bike ticket costs roughly CZK 45-65 per journey. On express (R) and fast services with a marked bike wagon the seat reservation, about CZK 35, is compulsory and capped, on the Český Krumlov line 194 and the Prague-Budějovice line 220 the summer slots go early. Regional Os trains take bikes without reservation, space permitting.

other.label: Rental
other.text: České Budějovice has both Rekola and Nextbike station-based bikes for city hops. For touring bikes and e-bikes, the Třeboň spa complexes Bertiny lázně and Lázně Aurora run guest fleets, and Top Bicycle and AVE Bicycle Tours deliver hire bikes and e-bikes anywhere in South Bohemia with a one-way drop.

other.label: Luggage transfer
other.text: Top Bicycle and AVE Bicycle Tours both move bags between South Bohemian towns for roughly €12-18 per bag per stage; book at least two weeks out.

other.label: Navigation
other.text: Czech cycle routes are signed with yellow route numbers on white; the Greenway Praha-Vídeň and EuroVelo 7 carry their own logos. KČT paper maps at 1:60,000 cost around CZK 130 at any information centre.

other.label: Pond dam access
other.text: Dams are working infrastructure owned by Rybářství Třeboň. Cycling on marked routes is fine; riding onto an unmarked dam during a harvest, when heavy machinery is on it, is not.

other.label: Protected area
other.text: Třeboňsko is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and a Ramsar site. Stay on tracks, keep out of reed beds, and do not fly a drone, Czech law requires registration and the reserve zones are restricted.

other.label: Opening traps
other.text: Czech castles close entirely November to March and on Mondays year-round. Visits are guided, timed and capped; buy the slot on arrival, not when you are ready.

proTips: Come in the last week of October for the výlov, the carp harvest. Rožmberk and Svět are drained on announced dates, the dams turn into a working festival and the fish goes straight from net to grill.
Book the Český Krumlov Baroque theatre tour the day you arrive in Třeboň, not the day you arrive in Krumlov. Visitor numbers are capped at a few dozen per tour to protect the machinery.
Order kapr na černo or a carp soup in Třeboň rather than at the Prague end of the trip. The fish comes from the pond you rode around that morning.
Use the Zlatá stoka towpath rather than the parallel road between Stará Hlína and Třeboň. It is traffic-free, packed sand, and the reason the canal exists is visible the whole way.
Buy your KČT map at the Třeboň information centre on the square on arrival. Czech route numbering does not always match what a phone app thinks the network looks like.

packingNotes: Tyres of 35-42 mm with some tread. The dams are packed sand and crushed limestone and turn soft after rain.
Mosquito repellent with DEET for the June and July reed margins; the Třeboň bogs are serious about this.
Binoculars, compact. This is one of Central Europe's best inland birding landscapes and the dams put you at eye level with the water.
Sunblock; there is no shade on a pond dam for kilometres at a time.
CZK cash in small notes for pubs, ferry-style pond crossings and information centres.
A spare tube and a patch kit, bike shops exist in Třeboň, Budějovice and Krumlov and essentially nowhere else on the route.
whatCouldGoWrong: **The bike wagon on the Krumlov line is full.** Summer Sunday services genuinely refuse bikes. Fallback: take an Os regional service, or ride the 25 km back to Budějovice on the Vltava path, which is flat and asphalt.

**Heavy rain turns the dam tops to mud.** Packed sand becomes unrideable after 24 hours of rain. Fallback: the Day 3 asphalt route via Chlum u Třeboně and Borovany substitutes for the Rožmberk day without losing distance.

**The carp harvest closes a dam.** During the výlov the working dams are shut to through traffic. Fallback: ride the outer ring of the pond system on asphalt and come back on foot to watch, which is the better experience anyway.
